properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured): the "shared record moved" hint named only what the file had that the graph lacked and recommended import_graph; the import's upsert then reverted three NEWER live edits to main's older copies — repairing "behind" by import undid "ahead"
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL, 2026-09-23, from the dev_reflow2 hub session.

① OBSERVED: three records edited in reflow2's shared live store on 2026-09-23 between 14:44 and 14:46 UTC by the session that built #578 — epoch:planned-the-composition-blockers-and-the-two-steps-that-were-passed-over (status arrived, rename, arrival note), fact:the-first-doubt-trace-on-reflow2-found-231-open-defect-findings-behind-126-settled-choices (a PARTLY SUPERSEDED note), dec:idea-the-design-gets-a-branch-dimension-for-implementation-facts (an evidence note and a CORRECTION) — later held main's older content exactly. Their preserved-on-write snapshots from those edits were still present (the epoch's :r2 holds status=arrived), so the writes had landed. NOT affected: nodes and edges created after main (57 of them, untouched), and every snapshot — upsert never deletes.

② PRECEDENT: searched ("import_graph upsert overwrote newer live edits reverted older export file clobber"). Nearest records are about an import from a NEWER reflow2 version (ver:an-import-knows-its-own-age); nothing covers an import that is older than the graph ON SOME NODES.

③④⑤ CANDIDATES AND THE MEASUREMENT THAT SEPARATED THEM: (a) the writes never landed — refuted, the post-main snapshots exist and :r2 captured status=arrived; (b) some other import or replace in the window — every Claude transcript for reflow2 and dev_reflow2 searched between 14:40 and 17:47 UTC: no import_graph, no --import; (c) the hub session's import_graph at 17:46:12 UTC of reflow2/docs/design/reflow2.json — at that moment the file equalled main (git status clean) and held these three nodes in their pre-edit form. A scan of the whole store for "current content equals main's but a preserved-on-write snapshot newer than main exists" finds exactly these three and no others, which is what (c) predicts and (b) would not bound. CAUSE: (c).

⑥ THE CLASS, not the instance. The loop hint on an ordinary read said "The shared record at … has moved since this graph synced with it, and holds 9 node(s) and 587 edge(s) this graph does not (…). To take them in, call import_graph with path …". The comparison is ONE-SIDED: it names what the FILE has that the graph lacks and never what the GRAPH has that is newer than the file — here, three edited nodes. And import_graph is an upsert that lets the document win on every id it names, with no check that the live node has moved past the incoming version, although the store holds the evidence (a preserved-on-write snapshot created after the document's content). So a file that is behind the graph on some nodes and ahead on others is reconciled by the one call that clobbers the "ahead" half, and the hint recommends that call. It would have fired on any session that followed the hint.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: exactly how the file came to hold main's copy while the store was ahead. The #578 session ran `git stash push docs/design/reflow2.json` → checkout/merge main → `git stash pop` at 14:43:45 UTC and the write-through then had to resume against a file that had changed under it; that sequence is the likely route and was not replayed. Also not established: whether the write-through had declined (the hand-edit guard) during the window. No fix is built here; the re-applied edits were made by the session that owned them, from its own transcript.

ESTABLISHED 2026-09-23, from the session that made the 14:43 git step (read back from its own transcript, not recalled): that step was "stash docs/design/reflow2.json IF it differs from HEAD, fast-forward main to origin/main (#578's squash merge a7ecfc1), pop the stash if one was made". No stash was made or left behind: `git stash list` holds no "live export after 578" entry, and `git status` right after showed the file clean. So the fast-forward alone replaced the working-tree export with main's #578 copy. The write-through HAD declined after it: the next loop_status (14:46:04) reported auto_export {exports: 0, skipped: "./docs/design/reflow2.json has changed since reflow2 last wrote it, so the write-through left it alone"}. The three edits made at 14:44–14:46 therefore reached the live store but not the file, and the file on disk was main's copy. That is consistent with the record-moved hint then reading the file as holding records the store lacked, which is what recommended the import.
